title: bin/cairn looks up a declared device name with one grep
intention: bin/cairn looks up a declared answers_as name with one grep over the device charters, so the dispatcher's happy path costs under the floor's 10 ms budget again.
why: Measured 2026-11-18: test_cairn_floor's happy path reads +17.6 to +21.6 ms at HEAD against a 10 ms budget. Bisected to 7ada27cdb (ticket 8c5fdb750b75), which dropped the instance-dir short-circuit, so a device that lives only in instance space runs 16 forked greps, one per charter. This is n=4 of 'a land leaves another proof's seal stale': 7ada27cdb landed without resealing test_cairn_floor.
traces_to: Law 8: nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build could not pass; Law 9: a deterministic red is fixed or carries a decision.
how: In bin/cairn, where $CLASS_ROOT/$device is absent, replace the per-charter grep loop with one grep -lE '^  "answers_as": "<device>",?$' over "$CLASS_ROOT"/*/intention+why.json, guarded with || true (set -euo pipefail ends the script on a no-match), taking the first file and its parent folder name as the device. bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py's PROVES gains this ticket's id, outcome 1 -> test_happy_path_costs_under_10ms.
